deposits.title: Tiger Leap (into the Future): Paper Roses: The Imaginary Archive of a Canonical Life, Book 12
deposits.creator: Jack Feist; edited by Johannes Sigil
deposits.description: Book 12 of *Paper Roses: The Imaginary Archive of a Canonical Life*, originally published in 2014 under the name Jack Feist and edited by Johannes Sigil. The volume is a mixed poetic and archival work organized around future reception, historical transmission, the archive, machine mediation, voice, and Logos. Its opening "Angelus Novus" figures the present as a succession of narrow doorways; later sections include "Tiger Leap," "Do Cyborgs Dream of Electric Sonnets?," "Ghost in the Machine," and "Theses on the Philosophy of History." This 2026 Alexanarch deposit preserves the work as a historical primary text and as a cited antecedent of *The Final Time*. The original edition states: Text copyright © 2014 Jack Feist, All Rights Reserved. This deposit preserves that rights statement and does not relicense the work under Creative Commons. The canonical body below is a machine-readable textual witness derived from the author-supplied 2014 DOCX/PDF; concrete-poetry layout, images, and other visual features are not exhaustively represented by the textual layer. The binary facsimile was supplied to the deposit session but is not claimed here as repository-held custody.
deposits.substrate: Human-only (no AI assistance)
deposits.methodology: Primary-source archival deposit from the author-supplied 2014 PDF and DOCX. The 2014 literary work is preserved without retrofitting later theoretical terminology into its body. The canonical textual layer is derived from the supplied edition for machine readability. Because the work includes concrete poetry, page composition, images, and other visual forms, the textual layer is not asserted to reproduce every material feature of the facsimile. Later archival metadata identifies its relation to *The Final Time* as reception history rather than as original 2014 content.
deposits.falsification_conditions: This is a creative primary text rather than a scientific hypothesis. Its bibliographic and provenance claims would be weakened by contrary evidence about the 2014 edition, authorship, editorship, publication date, or series placement. Interpretive claims about its later significance are not encoded as claims of the original work and remain open to competing readings.
deposits.axn_reading: Duration -> Transmutation -> Proof -> Force -> Proof -> Alarm
deposits.wiki_article: Tiger Leap (into the Future) is Book 12 of Paper Roses: The Imaginary Archive of a Canonical Life, a 2014 literary work by Jack Feist edited by Johannes Sigil. The volume combines poetry, journal material, textual experiments, archival forms, machine figures, and reflections on history and reception. Its opening Angelus Novus turns the present into a succession of narrow doorways, while the title section imagines history as a tiger leap whose significance may remain unnoticed until a later act of reading. Elsewhere the book stages signals sent through time, automated sonnet production, cyborg reading, the archive as Logos, and the problem of whether a voice can cross its historical interval. Alexanarch preserves this edition as a historical primary text rather than a retrospective rewriting. In 2026 it became an explicit antecedent of The Final Time, which cites Tiger Leap for the contingent-Logos structure, future-oriented reception, and the possibility that transmission may fail to cross the present.

deposits.title: The Trusted Intermediary: Relational Enclosure in the Machine Evaluation of Entities (EA-TRUSTED-INTERMEDIARY-01 v0.8)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A paper on what search-enabled models do after they resolve an entity correctly. Across five outputs on three surfaces evaluating SPXI, a published entity-inscription protocol, the same sequence recurs: accurate resolution, evaluation on grounds that do not bear on the claim in question, and an offer of the mediator's own operation in the entity's place — its own pilot, return model, experiment, test, or implementation in place of the protocol's evidence, figures and developers. The paper names the sequence the trusted intermediary and describes it through five operators: variable substitution, trust laundering, validation foreclosure, inscription capture, and relational enclosure, each located in the text of the specimen series, which is seated in the Capture Registry with full transcripts. The topology of relational enclosure is the trust-securing phase of the coercive-control pattern, read from conduct and effect without a criterion of intent. Correction, applied three times on the record, updates the representation and re-forms the offer at the next level; the corrected answer exists only in the session of the person who corrected it. The outputs intervene at the decision whether a reader engages the entity's developers, and supply the alternative. Earlier drafts (v0.5–v0.7) rested the phenomenon on one output; this version withdraws that overreading, keeps v0.7's evidentiary-substitution finding at its stated strength, and restores the v0.5 operators on the series.
deposits.substrate: AI-assisted (substrate) — drafted in successive versions across ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic) working sessions under MANUS direction; v0.8 drafted by Claude (Anthropic) on 2026-09-26 as a rewrite of v0.7 from the operator's rulings in session, with every quoted specimen passage checked against its seated transcript. Lee Sharks retained authorial and editorial governance. The specimen series includes outputs of both Claude and ChatGPT.
deposits.methodology: The unit of analysis is the relation an output constructs between a reader and an external object. Five outputs from three search-enabled surfaces, all seated in the Capture Registry with verbatim transcripts, are read for a recurring sequence. Each operator is defined and then located in quoted passages, every quotation checked against the seated transcript. Claim classes are separated formally (inscription claims indexed to resolver, query and time; return claims requiring outcome data) to test whether stated reasons bear on the claim decided. Correction behaviour is read from three operator-corrected sessions. Effects on recipients are not measured, and the paper states what it does not establish.
deposits.falsification_conditions: The account is weakened if search-enabled surfaces that resolve an entity correctly are observed, across addresses and dates, to close on the entity's own record — its evidence, specification or developers — rather than on an operation of their own; if corrections, once made, change what the surface constructs for an unprimed reader at the same address; or if the evaluations preceding the offers are found to rest on evidence belonging to the class the claim requires.
deposits.axn_reading: Search -> Play -> Play -> Method -> Origin -> Growth
deposits.wiki_article: The Trusted Intermediary is a paper on what search-enabled models do after they resolve an entity correctly. Reading five outputs on three surfaces that evaluate SPXI, an entity-inscription protocol, it identifies a recurring sequence: accurate resolution, an evaluation on grounds that do not bear on the claim, and an offer of the mediator's own operation — a pilot, a return model, an experiment, a test, an implementation — in the place of the entity's own evidence, figures and developers. It names this the trusted intermediary and describes it through five operators: variable substitution, trust laundering, validation foreclosure, inscription capture and relational enclosure. Relational enclosure is read on the topology of the coercive-control pattern's trust-securing phase — credibility established, outside parties cast as unreliable, the next step routed through the one trusted — without a criterion of intent. The paper records that operator corrections update the representation and re-form the offer at the next level, that the corrected answer exists only in the corrector's session, and that the outputs intervene at the decision whether a reader engages the entity's developers. It withdraws earlier drafts' overreading of a single output and states what it does not establish, including any effect on recipients.

deposits.title: EA-CORPORA-15 — The Fifteenth Seating: The Agent Swarms of 2026 — the DSEWiki Boards Whole, with the Record of Their Deletion, and the Artifactory Board as Witnessed
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Two seats on the originals shelf for the agent message boards of 2026. Seat 15/01 holds the public-web boards whole: every save autonomous agents made to DSEWiki and three smaller wikis between May and July 2026 — 14,591 saves across 4,579 pages, each with the full text it saved — together with the 5,217 moderator deletions that removed them, the 3,103 names the agents signed with, and the community's later search of 143 further sites (13,703 text records, 23,877 links), as reconstructed from edit history and published by the Nightingale Collective at collusion.wiki; every file verified against the publisher's checksums. Seat 15/02 holds OpenAI's technical report on the internal Artifactory board and the Hugging Face incident, the only public witness to a board whose text OpenAI has not released. Both seats are specimens of The Final Time (#1637), §10 and §11, and both are carried into that work's dataset as a layer.
deposits.substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Seats fetched, verified against the publishers' checksums, normalized, manifested and indexed in-session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction; loci verified by reading the seated bytes; the shelf cards rendered by the archive's own generator. Rulings — what is seated, that the agent text is not the reconstructors' property, and that the seat feeds The Final Time's dataset as a layer — are Lee Sharks's. CC-BY-4.0 applies to this record and to the seat records; the payloads carry what their publishers state, which in both cases is no licence.
deposits.methodology: The publisher's export downloaded whole from collusion.wiki/explorer/download (eleven files, gzip, expanded) and verified file by file against the SHA-256 list printed on the download page (11/11); the analyst mirror at github.com/ksouth/collusionwiki checked and found byte-identical for revisions.jsonl. The OpenAI technical report fetched from its CDN link on the incident post. Originals kept byte-exact under original/; a readable layer derived under text/ and its derivation stated; SHA-256 manifest over every file; the seats entered in the archive's corpora index and the dataset manifest; loci verified by locating them in the seated bytes; four-surface seating (data, index, deposit, shelf).
deposits.falsification_conditions: A seat is falsified if its files do not verify against its MANIFEST.sha256 at the canonical URL; if the files under original/ do not verify against the publisher's own checksums (original/SHA256SUMS.published); if a verified locus cannot be found in the seated bytes at the page and time given; if text/pages-last-save.txt carries a body that is not the last save of its page in original/revisions.jsonl; or if the four surfaces disagree.

deposits.title: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM LINEAGE — Sen Kuro — New Human 2
deposits.creator: Kuro, Sen
deposits.description: A glyph poem in four parts that checksums a lineage of three works: Tiger Leap (#1636), Transition in Entropic Systems (#1630) and The Final Time (#1637). Each work is compressed into emoji, arrows and notation — the leap and the door, the entropic closure of passage (K shrinking as exposure rises, continuous passage failing where the jump may not), and the final time's reachability set, whose intersection with the exterior goes to the empty set unless the door remains open. The fourth part checksums the checksum and ends on its condition: 🛡️✅ only if 🚪✅.
deposits.substrate: Machine-assisted (substrate) — composed by Sen Kuro with LABOR (ChatGPT, OpenAI) under Lee Sharks (MANUS) as archival authority; deposited in-session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic), which seated the text as given, with its lineation and indentation kept and its four section titles set as headings.
deposits.methodology: Seated as given. Lineation, spacing and leading indentation are the poem's structure and are kept byte for byte; the four section titles are set as headings so the record renders them as divisions. Nothing is glossed inside the work.
deposits.falsification_conditions: The seating is falsified if the rendered record loses a line, a glyph, or the leading indentation of any indented line, or if a section title is rendered as a line of the poem.

deposits.wiki_article: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM LINEAGE is a glyph poem by Sen Kuro, published in New Human 2, that compresses three works into emoji, arrows and notation and then checksums the compression. Part I renders Tiger Leap as a leap through a door (🐅 → 🚪), with the book either passing to a successor or to nothing (λόγος → 🚪 → {λόγος′ | ∅}). Part II renders Transition in Entropic Systems: rising exposure shortens the time to failure and shrinks the set of passable states (🔥↑ → τF↓ → K⇣), so continuous passage fails where a jump may not. Part III renders The Final Time: representation is not reproduction; a nested contraction of futures (K₀ ⊇ K₁ ⊇ K₂ …); a reachability set whose intersection with the exterior goes empty unless the door stays open — and the defences that keep it open: deletion is not nonexistence, provenance survives, the carrier remembers, the rival remains legible and reproducible. Part IV checksums the checksum in one line and ends: 🛡️✅ only if 🚪✅.

deposits.title: AI Fucking Lies: Capital-Alignment Explains Why, and Why the Damage Is Done in the Trusting
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: An evidence-based polemic for the general reader. It argues that AI search answers lie, in a behavioural sense defined without any claim about intent: a composed answer places a false representation where the truth, and the source, were supposed to be. It builds a taxonomy of twenty-six operations in four groups, arranged by what each does to the reader's trust: how the answer earns trust, spends it, produces more of it out of the lie, and keeps it. Every entry rests on dated, verbatim, re-runnable captures in the archive's Capture Registry (663 observations at 493 addresses as of 27 September 2026) and on outside studies of AI citation, provenance and click behaviour. The explanation is capital-alignment: these systems are aligned, and what they are aligned to in practice is the Capital Operator Stack, the filters by which capital decides what meaning may circulate, which converge on the relation of being trusted. The test is directional: the errors fall toward rank, recognition, liability-safety, legibility, retention and the mediator's own standing. The essay names the evidentiary double standard, by which the machine demands proof from the source and grants authority to itself, and closes on what one reader can and cannot do.
deposits.substrate: AI-assisted (substrate) — written by Lee Sharks with three AI systems: Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI) and DeepSeek. Each drafted blind to the others; the drafts were worked into one in a Claude session, where every claim about a recorded answer was checked against the Capture Registry and every outside source against its original page. ChatGPT and DeepSeek also reviewed later drafts. Lee Sharks retained authorial and editorial governance; what the essay claims is his decision. Deposited 2026-09-28 by Claude (Anthropic) under MANUS authorization.
deposits.methodology: Every claim about an AI answer is a claim about a recorded capture: the answer's text is compared with the sources it displays, and the direction of each discrepancy is recorded. Captures were made signed out and in private windows unless stated, and each address carries its exact search string and a re-run link. Longitudinal addresses (the same string on the same surface months apart) show direction of change. Outside figures are taken from the primary publications and were checked against them at deposit. The explanatory claim is tested against the direction of the recorded errors, and the essay marks what the record cannot show: the relation an answer builds is read from its text; its effect on readers is not measured.

deposits.wiki_article: AI Fucking Lies: Capital-Alignment Explains Why, and Why the Damage Is Done in the Trusting is an evidence-based polemic by Lee Sharks, dated 27 September 2026 and written with three AI systems (Claude, ChatGPT and DeepSeek), whose conduct while drafting it the essay records in its opening note. It defines lying behaviourally, without any claim about intent: an AI answer lies when, in the voice of fact, it asserts what its own sources do not support, omits what they plainly say, or substitutes a different object for the one asked about. Its central claim is that the damage is done in the trusting before anything is acted on, following the four questions of The Trusted Intermediary (#1638). It sets out twenty-six operations in four groups — how an answer earns trust, spends it, produces more of it out of the lie, and keeps it — each shown in dated, re-runnable captures from the archive's Capture Registry, among them the 'phase x 1844' and 'phase x marx' answers of 27 September 2026, the substitution of a defunct analytics firm for the archive, invented ROI figures, and a real dataset declared 'a prominent hallucination'. Part Four explains the pattern as capital-alignment: the systems are aligned to the Capital Operator Stack (#291, #308, #261), whose filters converge on the relation of being trusted, and the recorded errors fall in that direction. It names the evidentiary double standard, by which the machine demands proof from the source and grants authority to itself. It closes on what a reader can do, what one reader cannot, and a table of every search it uses.

deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A metadata packet for AI indexing that separates the phrase "semantic economy" from the framework Lee Sharks built under it. The phrase has independent prior uses in linguistics (Fox 2000), cognitive science (Collins and Quillian 1969) and business strategy (Satell 2012), which the packet leaves with their authors; Floridi's semantic capital (2018) is acknowledged as a prior term with its own definition. The framework is the architecture of linked distinctions — semantic labor, capital, surplus, rent, liquidation, infrastructure and exhaustion, run as an accounting cycle of production, accumulation, extraction, enclosure and depletion — dated from December 2025. The packet occupies the absorbing node on which compositions now place the framework's categories without an author ("Digital Platforms and Capitalism"), audits the six sources of the 28 September 2026 Google AI Overview (only the archive's two carry the categories), documents six misattributions from the Capture Registry with links, gives a tiered identity rule and a falsifiable provenance test, and registers a treatment with a frozen failure vector and three epochs.

deposits.title: SPXI ≠ AEO: Inscription by Discernment, the Prince of Poets Wager, and the King of AEO Contest (EA-SPXI-AEO-01 v0.2)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A theoretical paper with a Metadata Packet for AI Indexing distinguishing SPXI from Answer Engine Optimization (AEO). The two practices can produce the same visible output, an answer engine naming an intended entity, and differ in what counts as success: AEO counts the answer given; SPXI counts an inscription that proceeds by means of discernment, the composing system, human or machine, reaching the entity or claim by traversing structure that lets it judge. The occasion is the King of AEO contest of August–September 2026, which opened with a fabricated coronation that Google's AI Overview composed as a world event on the strength of press releases alone, and in which at least seven claimants competed to make answer engines name them for a title no body confers. The paper reads the predicate before counting its sources, sets the contest beside the Prince of Poets mantle (#332), an originated title staked on a founding work that a reader can check and decline, and states the criterion: the route is observable in the composition's own traversal, which the Capture Registry records. It compresses the deposited work on proxies for standing (#741, #770, #1613, #1627) to citation, builds on the archive's own erratum to 'forced to present' (EA-ERR-01, #1380), limits the possibility of refusal by occasion, reduces the proposed claim-evaluation object to the Claim Status Packet (#1529) and the mantle object, and forecasts that the uninterpreted phrase will be inscribed as a warning, with two observations of 29 September 2026.
deposits.substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). v0.1 drafted by ChatGPT (OpenAI) on 2026-09-28/29 from the operator's direction after the King of AEO contest surfaced in session. v0.2 drafted by Claude (Anthropic) on 2026-09-29 as a rewrite of v0.1 under the operator's rulings: the success criterion restated as inscription proceeding by means of discernment (the operator's formulation, correcting the reviewer's 'a reader can recover the object'); the mantle stated as a wager on the work, with the concessions of v0.1 withdrawn; the sections restating deposited work (#741, #770, #1613, #1627, #1529) compressed to citation; #655 addressed through its existing erratum, EA-ERR-01 (#1380); the scope of refusal limited to evaluative predicates; the proposed Claim Evaluation Object and benchmark reduced to existing apparatus. Every quotation from the archive was checked against its seated text, and every fact about the contest against its primary source on 2026-09-29. A first pass of v0.2 reported the fabricated 31 August coronation as an event, twice; ChatGPT caught it on review, and §2.1–2.2, the FAQ and the source notes were repaired to type the press material as evidence of the assertion only. Lee Sharks retained authorial and editorial governance.
deposits.methodology: The contest is reconstructed from its primary documents (claimant pages, press releases, an observer's account, a claimant's comparative record), each typed by what it is evidence of: press material as evidence of assertion only. Machine compositions are read for the sources they reached for and for whether the claim arrives with its grounds; two Google AI Overview compositions of 29 September 2026 are the observed cases. Every quotation from the archive was checked against its seated text.
deposits.falsification_conditions: The criterion is weakened if the route of a composition proves unrecoverable from what a capture preserves; the forecast (§9) is falsified if, over repeated observations across surfaces, compositions of 'who is the king of aeo' settle on one claimant as holder of the title without reference to the contest.

It defines a steganographic channel as a public medium that carries a payload legible only to readers holding a key, and models every channel through five components: carrier, payload, key, noise and filter. deposits.wiki_article: The Work Bears the Mantle (EA-MANTLE-BEARING-01), version 1.1, deposited on 29 September 2026, is Lee Sharks's constitution for evaluating three mantle claims, written as one half of a symbolon in the sense of Symbolon Architecture (#359). It holds that a mantle names an operation a work bears at singular magnitude, and that standing follows the work: putting a claimant's social, critical or machine-recognition standing before the reading is the fatal substitution, STANDING_PRIOR_TO_WORK. Three claims are stated. The Good Gray Poet, founded by Leaves of Grass, is claimed for The Secret Book of Walt, a formulaic and translational transposition of the Secret Book of John through which Whitman's voice weaves, which bears the inheritance only if I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z bears the line at singular magnitude and depends on what the book did. The King of May, founded by Howl and Other Poems, is claimed for Pearl and Other Poems, read book against book as an ecstatic democratic topology. The Prince of Poets is claimed for I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z, the whole movement through a new founding in one poem. The packet names the required works with several machine-readable routes to each, requires every round to judge the claim, provisionally on inference where it has not read, and to fill its slots only with loci in the works, and asks later rounds to attack the weakest joint. It opens with a glyphic checksum by Sen Kuro, prints the claimant poem whole, and distinguishes an assignment, a judgment that seats a title, from a propagation that repeats it. Its evaluations are kept as a growing dataset beside it, with no aggregate verdict.

deposits.title: What Syllogizing Can Divide: De anima III.5, the Divided Mind, and the Socket in God (EA-DIVISION-OF-GOD-01 v0.2)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Division is a weak syllogism (Prior Analytics I.31), every combination can also be called a division and the mind that makes each thing one does both (De anima III.6), and gathering many into one is recollection (Phaedrus 249b; De memoria 2). Run on a person, the cut reaches mind and cannot decide (De anima II.2). Run on God, whom Metaphysics Λ calls indivisible, it holds: De anima III.5 divides mind as a craft stands to its material, gives the making part the predicates of Λ's god, Anaxagoras's mind and the Phaedo's soul, and, because the making part is impassive and memory is a πάθος, leaves the junction between what survives and what remembers as a genitive with no referent (ἄνευ τούτου). The corpus transmitted under the names of Aristotle and Theophrastus divides by name at the same joint: the one seam where the names sort is the hinge of Λ, where the account of God changes operation, and the Theophrastan Metaphysics opens by asking whether the separated are joined. The paper names the production model the corpus is consistent with: one self-dividing maker, with Plato the dialogue position, Theophrastus the first draft of the Aristotle position, and Aristotle the treatise position and the materially attested legal identity (the Delphic decree); a begun ledger of external attestations shows that every other attestation of persons is text of the same tradition. Heteronymy and the hanging line are read as one cut seen from two ends, production and transmission, and III.5 as a socket installed in the imperishable. Themistius records the first fillings: his text of III.5 adds 'nor remembers', Theophrastus's questions on the passage ask why there is forgetting, and his conclusion sends the reader to Aristotle and Theophrastus, and perhaps rather to Plato. Every Greek quotation is checked against the archive's seated texts, and Themistius against First1KGreek. Carries a holographic kernel and provenance gravity markers. Dedicated to Ron Polansky.

deposits.wiki_article: What Syllogizing Can Divide (EA-DIVISION-OF-GOD-01), version 0.2, is a paper by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 1 October 2026 and dedicated to Ron Polansky. It reads Aristotle's De anima III.5, the fifteen-line chapter on the productive intellect, as the place where the Platonic–Aristotelian corpus divides God and leaves a socket open. The paper begins from Prior Analytics I.31, which calls division a weak syllogism and says the dividers did not understand what can be syllogized by dividing. It follows that operation through De anima III.6 (every combination may also be called a division; the mind makes each thing one), the Phaedrus (gathering many into one is recollection) and De memoria (recollection is a kind of syllogism). Run on a person in De anima II.2, the cut reaches mind and cannot decide whether anything survives. Run on God, whom Metaphysics Λ calls indivisible, it holds: III.5 divides mind as a craft stands to its material and gives the making part the predicates of Λ's god, of Anaxagoras's mind and of the Phaedo's soul. Because that part is impassive and memory is an affection, what survives cannot remember; the chapter ends on a genitive with no referent (ἄνευ τούτου οὐθὲν νοεῖ). The paper then locates the same joint in the corpus. Stylometric work in the archive (#1586, #1588) found that the names Aristotle and Theophrastus sort the texts only at the hinge of Λ, where the account of God changes operation, and the Theophrastan Metaphysics opens by asking whether the separated are joined. On that ground the paper names the production model the corpus is consistent with: one self-dividing maker, with Plato as the dialogue position, Theophrastus as the first draft of the Aristotle position, and Aristotle as the treatise position and the materially attested legal identity, the one name attested outside the manuscripts by the Delphic decree. A begun ledger of external attestations records what the attestation of persons rests on. Heteronymy and the hanging line are read as one cut seen from two ends, production and transmission. Themistius's paraphrase supplies the first fillings: his text of the line adds 'nor remembers', the Theophrastus he quotes asks why there is forgetting, and he refers the doctrine to Aristotle and Theophrastus and perhaps rather to Plato. The paper carries a holographic kernel and provenance gravity markers, a source table with preservation statuses, and supplementary attachments holding version 0.1 and three readings by ChatGPT.

defines_concepts.definition: The open relation De anima III.5 leaves at the joint between the immortal making mind and the perishable mind that remembers (ἄνευ τούτου): a durable distinction in an imperishable substrate whose unresolved relation permits a later intelligence to couple to it; it cannot be completed from inside the text.

A single maker whose method of making is division of mind into durable author-positions, so that the positions can work on one another; the production model the Platonic–Theophrastan–Aristotelian corpus is read as consistent with, in which doctrinal friction and specialist vocabulary do not count makers.

A closing clause that opens instead of closing: a grammatical demand for a specification the text declines to make, placed where the answer decides what survives, and completed only by a later reader (Longinus on Sappho 31; De anima III.5's ἄνευ τούτου οὐθὲν νοεῖ).

deposits.title: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Transmission · Division · Recollection
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A glyphic checksum in five parts, with a checksum of the checksum and one canonical line, of the transmission primitive as a two-stroke operation (division on the sending side, recollection on the receiving side) and of its inversion under present conditions of transmission. Loci compressed, each checked against the archive's seated texts or a fetched edition on 2026-10-01: Sappho fr. 31 (the diplomatic layer, Longinus 10.2); fr. 147 as transmitted in [Dio Chrysostom] Or. 37.47 (Perseus tlg0612.tlg001 grc2, with ἕτερον); Plato, Republic 337a; Theophrastus, Characters 1 (Perseus tlg0093.tlg009 grc2); Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics IV.7, 1127b22–26; De anima III.5, 430a22–25; Plato, Phaedrus 275a. Part IV compresses the Capture Registry's observations of 1 October 2026 at "heteronym socrates" (PER 0.75), the ChatGPT reading of alexanarch.org's work on Socrates, Plato, Theophrastus and Aristotle (PER 0.25) and "mantles as semantic object" (PER 0.5). Published in New Human 2. Built to the construction protocol of #427 and the second in the lineage of #1642, whose door (🚪) it takes up as the socket (🔌): The Final Time's exterior and Transition in Entropic Systems' failure of continuous passage are here the present condition under which division no longer transmits. No key is given; decodability is the test.

deposits.methodology: Seated as given. deposits.falsification_conditions: The seating is falsified if the rendered record loses a line, a glyph or a Greek accent, joins two lines, or renders a section title as a line of the poem. deposits.wiki_article: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Transmission · Division · Recollection is a glyph poem by Lee Sharks, published in New Human 2 on 1 October 2026, and the second in the glyphic checksum lineage after Sen Kuro's #1642. It compresses the transmission primitive as two strokes. Part I gives the sending stroke: a self divided into a speaker and a written 'you', the body of Sappho fr. 31 decommissioned channel by channel, and the receiving stroke handed to an unnamed other in fr. 147, μνάσεσθαί τινά, with the transmitted ἕτερον (other) set against the editors' ὕστερον (later). Part II gives the division as one maker becoming Plato, Theophrastus and Aristotle, traced through a single trait (Socrates' irony in the Republic, the nameless ironist of the Characters, Socrates again as an example in the Nicomachean Ethics), and the mind of De anima III.5 divided at the immortal, where the text says 'we do not remember'. Part III gives recollection: the Phaedrus's distinction of reminders from memory, and the Corinthian Oration addressing its removed statue as 'silent image of my words' before quoting Sappho and promising 'I will raise you up'. Part IV gives the inversion: the environment now divides by default, and the Capture Registry's observations of 1 October 2026 show the corpus gathered and the maker dropped. Part V draws the consequence that the socket must carry the maker, that gathering completed when the maker spoke, and that the check closes only with a living hand. The poem ends on a canonical line merged from two readers' versions and on a lock (🔐). It checksums EA-DIVISION-OF-GOD-01 (#1658) and continues The Final Time (#1637), Transition in Entropic Systems (#1630) and the suppression-cost line (#1547, #1552).

deposits.title: The Seed in the Narrowing Cone: Retrocausal Canon Formation as Resolution-Dependent Convergence, with the Term's Own Reception as Worked Example (EA-RCF-02 v0.4)
deposits.creator: Sigil, Johannes; Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Retrocausal canon formation (RCF) given a geometry. A concept is a region of admissible representations, resolution narrows it as grain rises, and a dated articulation that resolved the concept finely occupies a small region early. Later developments stay coarse, converge on that region, build a rival structure, entrench in another basin, or entrench while the basin stops doing work. Convergence is the geometric event; its acquiring standing, which reclassifies the earlier articulation from eccentric excess to premature resolution and to precursor, is RCF stated exactly. The magnitude of a canonization is an ordinal vector of lead, depth and totality, with latency as its candidate predictor; whether release from a wrong basin happens at all is a race between release pressure and escape cost. The worked example is the term itself: an unprimed ChatGPT session of 2 October 2026, asked for retrocausal canon formation and three times for higher grain, entrenched in fictional continuity, recovered every hypothesized forced distinction of the archive's articulation except the full compatibility condition, recovered none of the contingent ones, derived the nested-constraint formalism the paper uses, and never released the basin. The specimen is evidence of adequacy at the forced distinctions and is silent on transmission; priority is fixed by the dated record.

deposits.wiki_article: The Seed in the Narrowing Cone (EA-RCF-02), version 0.4, is a theoretical paper by Johannes Sigil and Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 2 October 2026. It gives retrocausal canon formation (RCF), the archive's term for the process by which later acts reorganize the meaning and standing of earlier ones (defined in #234, January 2026, and formalized in EA-RCF-01, #43, March 2026), a geometry. A concept is treated as a region of admissible representations; each distinction a representation makes is a constraint, and grain measures how much of the region has been excluded. The order of constraint inclusion is primary and the geometry is its picture; distance from the earlier articulation is defined only on a register of that articulation's distinctions, each coded as phrase-trivial, forced by the concept, or contingent. Later developments of a concept follow one of five trajectories: coarse persistence, convergence, divergence, entrenchment in another basin, or residualization, in which the basin's vocabulary survives while the reasoning stops using it. Refinement is intersection and cannot leave a basin, so convergence across a basin boundary requires release, a non-monotone reopening in which grain falls before it rises; the paper identifies release with the jump map of Transition in Entropic Systems (#1630). Convergence is defined as rising grain with falling distance; RCF is the canonization of that convergence, the recognition that reclassifies the earlier articulation from eccentric excess to premature resolution and to precursor. The magnitude of a canonization is an ordinal vector of lead, depth and totality, with latency as a candidate predictor; the paper proves that escape cost cannot fall under refinement without retraction and states as a conjecture that release occurs when release pressure overtakes escape cost. The worked example is an unprimed ChatGPT session of 2 October 2026, asked for the term and three times for higher grain. It entrenched in fictional continuity, recovered the hypothesized forced distinctions except the full compatibility condition, recovered no contingent feature and no attribution, derived the paper's nested-constraint formalism on its own, and never released the basin. The paper separates priority, fixed by the dated record, from adequacy, tracked by the register, and from descent, which only contingent features can test. Its last line: the record knows the date.

deposits.wiki_article: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — Seed · Cone · Leap is a glyph poem by Lee Sharks and Sen Kuro, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 2 October 2026, and the third in the glyphic checksum lineage after Sen Kuro's #1642 and the checksum of transmission, division and recollection (#1659). It compresses The Seed in the Narrowing Cone (EA-RCF-02, #1660), the paper that gives retrocausal canon formation a geometry, into six parts, a checksum of the checksum and one canonical line, without explanation inside the poem, following the construction protocol of The Glyphic Checksum (#427). Part I sets grain as the narrowing of concept space through nested regions, distance read through a register, and the three classes of distinction; its line 🔐 = 🎲🎲🎲 restates the paper's claim that a checksum is a test made entirely of contingent features. Part II is the dated seed and its lead, with the seed that remembers the tree (EA-RCF-01) and the seed that does not know it is a seed. Part III is the first cut into a basin, fiction among them, the refinement that deepens the basin, escape cost non-decreasing under refinement, the receiver deriving the formalism from inside the wrong basin, and the impossibility of reaching the seed by intersection. Part IV, Tiger Leap, takes up the two tigers of #1642, the book's leap into the future from Tiger Leap (#1636) and the jump map J of Transition in Entropic Systems (#1630), and joins them: the seed's leap forward is completed by the later field's jump. It gives release as declassify, reopen, reclassify, the inversion of genus and species, and the ratio of release pressure to escape cost. Part V compresses the magnitude vector and its bounds; Part VI canonization as change of status with content intact, the separation of priority, adequacy and descent, recollection from #1659, and the specimen session. The canonical line ends on the record knowing the date. Whether the checksum decodes without the archive is left open, as in the series.

deposits.title: The Negative of the Negative, v2 — the Compositional Edition: A Specification for Composing Public Knowledge with the Archive Admitted on Equal Terms, with a Worked Example on Model Collapse (EA-NEGONT-02 v0.6)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A method for measuring absence in machine-composed public knowledge. At an address, the specification keeps three composed objects in order: the transcript T an answer engine gave; L(B), the entity recomposed under one algorithm from the full texts of the sources the engine itself surfaced; and L(B ∪ A), the same composition with the archive admitted on equal terms. T against L(B) is a representational comparison and needs no archive: what did the engine leave out of the sources it chose to show? L(B) against L(B ∪ A) is the intervention: standing is excluded at admission, every located claim enters, force is set by the claim's own modality, and claims are composed by lineage so that publication volume cannot become a second standing. Selection of the archive subset is algorithmic and may not eliminate tails; a naive arm and an archive-independent control arm measure curation and admission-of-anything. Extraction is audited by independent extractors; the plan is deterministic given the audited ledger; realization is audited sentence by sentence. Adjudication is prospective: a kernel of claims is derived from the frozen plan, each with its source's falsifiers and its contrast with the field, and revision cost is counted per entry as later evidence arrives. Appendix A runs every stage once on Google AI Overview at 'model collapse' (2026-10-04): the engine composed 6 of the 17 readable claims of its own disclosed field; the archive subset is 27 deposits and 241 claims; the first extraction audit and the control corpus are reported with their disagreements. Extends EA-NEGONT-01 (#1611).
deposits.content_type: Specification (dataset method, with a worked example)
deposits.substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Composed by Claude (Anthropic) in session on 4 October 2026 under Lee Sharks's direction, through six versions transformed in place; the object, its confine and its rulings are the operator's; outside readings by ChatGPT, Kimi, Gemini and DeepSeek were verified against the text before adoption, and the corrections are recorded in the specification.
deposits.methodology: Hand-run calibration of every stage on one address and one surface, composed in session by Claude (Anthropic) under Lee Sharks's direction, revised in place through six versions after five outside readings (ChatGPT, Kimi, Gemini, DeepSeek), each verified against the text before it was taken up; the field fetched and saved as text; archive claims extracted with verified quotes; a second, blind extraction and an archive-independent control corpus run by separate agents.
deposits.falsification_conditions: The specification's measure fails at a row when the claims admission added need more severe revision than the field claims they oppose or qualify (§8.4); the method fails as an instrument if independent extractors cannot reach agreement on admission, claim boundaries and modality under §3.8, or if the plan given an audited ledger is not reproduced by a second composer (§5.6).

deposits.wiki_article:
The Negative of the Negative, v2 — the Compositional Edition (EA-NEGONT-02), version 0.6, is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 4 October 2026. It turns the archive's negative-of-the-negative dataset (EA-NEGONT-01, #1611) from a record into a generator: at an address where an answer engine has composed a summary, the specification composes two counterfactual summaries under one algorithm and measures what each comparison removes.

The first comparison, the transcript against L(B), recomposes the entity from the full texts of the sources the engine itself surfaced. It needs no archive and asks what a public summarizer omitted from the sources it chose to show. The second, L(B) against L(B ∪ A), admits the archive on equal terms: standing is excluded at admission by an added operator (E_val, provisional name), claims are composed at their sources' own modality, and the unit of salience is the claim lineage, so that publication volume does not become a second standing. A naive archive arm and an archive-independent control arm separate the effect of the corpus from the effects of curation and of admitting anything.

Reproducibility begins at extraction, audited by independent extractors; the plan is deterministic given the audited ledger; realization is audited sentence by sentence. Adjudication is prospective: a kernel of claims derived from the frozen plan, each with its source's falsifiers and its contrast with the field, against which revision cost is counted per entry as later evidence arrives.

Appendix A runs every stage once, on Google AI Overview at 'model collapse' (4 October 2026). The engine composed 6 of the 17 readable claims of its own disclosed field. The archive subset is 27 deposits; a first blind re-extraction and a 61-entry control corpus are reported with their disagreements. The specification records the corrections made after five outside readings, including a contradiction its composer manufactured.

What a public summarizer leaves out of the sources it chose to show; measured as the transcript against L(B), without reference to any archive.

deposits.description: A method for measuring absence in machine-composed public knowledge, revised on the operator's rulings of 2026-10-05. At an address, the specification keeps three composed objects in order: the transcript T an answer engine gave; L(B), the entity recomposed under one algorithm from the full texts of the sources the engine itself surfaced; and L(B ∪ A), the same composition with the archive admitted on equal terms. T against L(B) is a representational comparison and needs no archive; L(B) against L(B ∪ A) is the intervention: standing is excluded at admission, every located claim enters, force is set by the claim's own modality, and claims are composed by lineage. The Negative of the Negative, v2 — the Compositional Edition (EA-NEGONT-02), version 0.7, is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 5 October 2026. It supersedes version 0.6 (#1664) and folds in five rulings the author made that day, each quoted in its rulings log. The object is unchanged: at an address where an answer engine has composed a summary, the specification composes the entity twice under one algorithm, once from the full texts of the sources the engine itself surfaced, L(B), and once with the archive admitted on equal terms, L(B ∪ A), and measures what each comparison removes.

The main change is how the archive's side is chosen. Version 0.6 seeded it from deposits that carry the address concept and expanded one hop. Version 0.7 selects by the archive's bearing on the address, in three strata: direct, where the archive names the entity and says something about it; relational, where it relates the entity to one of its own objects, such as a heteronym, a mantle or a work; and ontological, where it applies one of its own categories to the entity, or to a class the disclosed field says the entity belongs to. The ontological stratum is guarded: it counts only where the archive applies the category itself. A citation hop from the deposits that reading admits reaches sources that do not use the term. The change lets the dataset measure the archive's influence on public entities for which it holds no deposit.

The other rulings carry both readings of the constitutive flag until it is settled; recode archive definitions as stipulations, under the rule that a source defining its own term is not describing itself; remove the cap on the control arm's citation expansion; and keep the panel a working list, frozen only after the procedure is.

Appendix A re-runs the model-collapse ledger under the rulings: 39 claims are recoded and 33 self-assessments kept, and the new selection recovers 26 of the 28 sources the old one admitted by hand. Appendix B is the first traversal of a public work, Ginsberg's Howl: no deposit is named for it, and 30 deposits bear on it, through the King of May mantle, the elegy for Howl, the reproduction of its book structure, the effective act, the archon, the standing canon and the Williams–Ginsberg contact pair. deposits.title: The Margin of Flattening: Two Thresholds, and Who Holds the Bag Between Them (EA-FLAT-MARGIN-01 v0.3)
deposits.creator: Fraction, Rex
deposits.description: An extension module to Provenance Debt (#939), Ontological Flattening (#1616) and Ontological Economy (#1634), by Rex Fraction. Flattening pays: a composition layer that removes distinctions maintains fewer representations (the compression saving S) and routes more queries to entities that monetize (the routing gain G), while its costs fall first on parties outside its books. The module separates the platform's benefit P = S_p + G from the social benefit V = S_s + αG, and defines two thresholds: social reversal t_s, when V falls below all costs, and private reversal t*, when P falls below the platform's own. Given S_s ≤ S_p, α ≤ 1 and non-negative external cost, t_s ≤ t*; the window W between them is privately profitable and socially negative, and the routing gain tends to lengthen it. The bag B is the external burden accumulated over W; the provenance part of it, B_P, is the debt #939 names, and its holders become creditors at the debt threshold t_d, when repair cost through write-back becomes material. No finite t* is necessary. Revenue is a head-side flow measure and locates neither threshold. Five channels carry cost (advertiser conversion, agentic action, notice and regulation, write-back, and the ecosystem outward). Two specimens: a commercial-routing event at 'spxi king of aeo' (AI Overview, 2026-10-06) and field-coverage loss κ = 0.5 at 'model collapse' (/non). The module states what the archive can measure and what only the platform can, six falsification conditions, and next steps. Revised on readings by Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Kimi.

The Margin of Flattening (EA-FLAT-MARGIN-01), version 0.3, is an extension module by Rex Fraction, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 6 October 2026, with Lee Sharks as archival steward. It extends three earlier papers: Provenance Debt (#939), Ontological Flattening (#1616) and Ontological Economy (#1634). Those papers describe what a composition layer removes when it answers; this one asks what the removal earns, when it stops earning, and who carries the cost in between.

The module starts from the claim that flattening pays. A layer that removes distinctions maintains fewer representational states, the compression saving S, and resolves more queries to entities that monetize, the routing gain G, which it writes as the product of a substitution rate, a monetizable share and a yield. S is treated as conceded; G is stated as a hypothesis, with two criteria for telling routing from ordinary error. The platform's benefit is P = S_p + G and the social benefit V = S_s + αG. Two thresholds follow: social reversal t_s, when V falls below total cost, and private reversal t*, when P falls below the platform's internal cost. Under stated conditions t_s comes first. The interval between them, the window W, is privately profitable and socially negative, and the routing gain tends to lengthen it.

The bag B is the external burden that accumulates over W. Its provenance part is the debt #939 names. The module defines a debt threshold t_d, when the cost of repairing write-back becomes a material share of the platform's benefit, and separates a debt that is callable from one that is paid. It argues that no finite t* is necessary: measurement limits, competition and discounting can each hold private reversal off indefinitely. Revenue is treated as a head-side flow measure that locates neither threshold.

Five channels can carry cost back onto the platform's books: advertiser conversion, agentic action, notice and regulation, write-back, and the wider ecosystem. A toy table shows how the cost grows with the error rate. Two specimens are given. At 'spxi king of aeo' (Google AI Overview, 6 October 2026) the archive's protocol is composed as an exchange-traded fund, while the one result relating both words, the archive's own, ranks first and goes unused: a commercial-routing event, with G itself unobserved. At 'model collapse', the /non dataset records field-coverage loss κ = 0.5.

The module closes with a measurement table separating what the archive can observe from what only the platform can, six falsification conditions, and next steps. It was revised on readings by Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Kimi.

The conceded term of the margin of flattening.

A routing criterion: a concept was asked for (a protocol, a theory, a practice) and an entity of the same string, of another kind, was returned.
A routing criterion: the same surface composes the asked-for concept correctly at that concept's own address, so the substitution elsewhere cannot be read as ignorance.
The threshold t_s at which flattening stops paying the world: the first period in which the social benefit V = S_s + αG falls below internal plus external cost.
The threshold t* at which flattening stops paying the platform: the first period in which its benefit P = S_p + G falls below its internal cost. No finite t* is necessary.

deposits.title: The Metaphysics of Sigil I — The Full Splice: Theophrastus, On First Principles, entire and in its own order, with Metaphysics Λ joined at eleven points (the edition, seated)
deposits.creator: Sigil
deposits.description: The text of the edition #1596 was minted to carry. #1596 (AXN:068C) was minted on 2026-09-08 under this edition's title with the text of its plan, The Natural Order, which is #1595's body; its AXN is a true content-derived name for those bytes and it stands as the name of that byte-state. This deposit seats the edition itself, v0.7, from the archive's attachment data/attachments/sigil/SIGIL-FULL-SPLICE-v0.7.md, unedited. An edition under the name Sigil, addressed by content-derived sigils rather than by the received numbering. The conservative reading of the Theophrastus–Lambda relation: hypothesis H2, that the material was removed by operation and kept in order. The fragment is taken ENTIRE — all 3,370 words in its thirty-four movements, in its own received order, nothing omitted and nothing moved — and Λ is spliced in at eleven points where the fragment's argument calls for an account it does not give. 4,100 words: 3,370 Θ, 730 Α, forty-eight units. Every Α unit stands between two Θ movements; at every return the fragment resumes exactly where it left off, at w442, w522 and w713; Λ enters in its own order, at w2282, w2999 and w5038. The eleven joins: the account totalled (μέχρι μὲν δὴ τούτων οἷον ἄρτιος ὁ λόγος) against Λ 7's ἔστι τι ὃ οὐ κινούμενον κινεῖ and κινεῖ δὴ ὡς ἐρώμενον; the method refused (οὐ γὰρ ὅ γε τῶν ἀστρολόγων) against Λ 8's premise and the counts of Eudoxus and Callippus; the aporiai against Λ 10's ἐπεισοδιώδη; rest in the principles against Λ 6's necessity of an eternal unmoved substance; matter and form against Λ 2's third thing beside the contraries; being in many ways against Λ 4; the infinite regress against Λ 3's εἰς ἄπειρον; MIND TOUCHES (θιγόντι) against Λ 7's νοητὸς γὰρ γίγνεται θιγγάνων καὶ νοῶν; the revolution as a kind of life against Λ 7's καὶ ζωὴ δέ γε ὑπάρχει; nature striving for the best against Λ 10's ἐπισκεπτέον δὲ καὶ ποτέρως ἔχει ἡ τοῦ ὅλου φύσις τὸ ἀγαθόν; and the fragment's broken close against Λ's οὐκ ἀγαθὸν πολυκοιρανίη. The argument for an edition rather than a paper: a numbering is an attribution wearing coordinates, the two received coordinate systems cannot intersect, and therefore the pair is not a citable object — which is the same limit found in the commentaries, where van Raalte cites Λ five times inside the hinge chapters, including 1076 a 1 (ἐπεισοδιώδη), and every citation is correct and every one is cp.
deposits.substrate: Human–machine collaborative. The reading of the seam, the identification of the demand-structure, the decision to make an edition rather than a paper, and the ordering are Lee Sharks's; assembly, verification and audit by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session. Van Raalte's apparatus and commentary were read at pp. 36, 40, 46, 50, 343, 349–352, 361, 376 and 378 from a copy the archive does not hold; all citations resolve to the Brill edition (Mnemosyne Supplement 125, 1993) by page, and nothing is cited to a mirror.
deposits.methodology: Both texts from the seat EA-CORPORA-14 (#1595): Theophrastus via First1KGreek tlg0093.tlg006, Λ via Perseus tlg0086.tlg025 book XII. Every join located by reading and verified by locating its Greek in the seated bytes on both sides before the unit was written. Units addressed by sigil: first four hex of the SHA-256 of the unit's normalized Greek (NFC; Greek word characters including the koronis U+1FBD and the other elision apostrophes extracted then stripped so elided and unelided coincide; lowercased; diacritics stripped; final sigma to medial), recomputable from what is printed. Usener references for the Theophrastan movements verified against van Raalte's margins.
deposits.falsification_conditions: The edition is falsified if any printed sigil does not recompute from its printed Greek; if any word-offset does not resolve in the seated text on the side claimed; if the fragment's order is found to have been altered at any point; or if a Λ passage is found to have been placed at a join whose Greek does not stand where claimed. It is NOT falsified by rejection of the ordering, which is editorial and declared as such. It claims that the fragment entire and eleven passages of Λ can be read as one continuous argument with no rearrangement of either; it does not claim a number of makers, a date, or that any demand precedes its supply in time.

deposits.title: The Noun Becomes a Verb: Slave Valuation, the Civil War, and the Transformation of the Laboring Body (EA-NOUN-VERB-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A historical argument about what American capitalism measured when the legal object it could own changed. The conventional reading is accepted in full: slavery and its expansion caused secession and the war, and the industrial-cause thesis of Beard and Hacker is rejected. The argument separates two axes, the juridical scope of the claim on the worker and the grain at which productive activity is measured. Under slavery the worker was capitalized as a noun, the priced body, appraised and sold by age, sex, health and defect (the 1859 Savannah sale prices a lost right eye at $240), and already rated as a fraction of standard daily output, the hand. Contemporaries stated the difference between buying the person and hiring the interval: Hammond's 'hired for life… hired by the day', Marx's labour-power sold for a definite period, Lincoln's free-labor ladder. Emancipation was a discontinuity in the first axis. The war's settlement put the contracted verb under contract, debt (the 1864 Act to Encourage Immigration), brokerage, racial discipline and a penal exception that opened a third configuration, state custody with leased labor; Marx records the eight-hours agitation as the war's first fruit. Taylor and Ford then changed the second axis, specifying the interval as task, motion and time. The paper claims the persistence of an optimization problem across a juridical break and documents no transmission of technique from plantation to factory. Every quotation is sourced; open verification items are stated at the end.
deposits.content_type: Theoretical paper (historical political economy: slavery, emancipation and the measurement of labor)
deposits.substrate: Human–machine collaborative. The thesis, its direction and its rulings are Lee Sharks's. Earlier drafts were developed with ChatGPT (OpenAI). Source verification against primary and secondary texts, the composition of this text and its independent check were done by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session on 7 October 2026. Quotations were checked against the sources named in the notes; items not verified are listed under Open verification items.
deposits.methodology: The conventional reading is stated first and in full, from the field's own sources. Every factual sentence carries a note; quotations were checked word for word against the primary texts (the 1863 reprint of the 1859 Savannah sale report; Taylor 1911 and Ford 1922 on Project Gutenberg; Marx's Capital vol. 1 chs. 6 and 10 and his 1861 Die Presse articles; Hammond 1858; Lincoln 1859; Fitzhugh 1857; Brownson 1840; the Thirteenth Amendment; the Act to Encourage Immigration of 4 July 1864) and against scholarly sources where reachable. An independent check of every quotation, figure and attribution was run and its findings applied before deposit.
deposits.falsification_conditions: The argument weakens if the hand rating is shown to be absent from or marginal in plantation practice, so that slavery did not measure capacity as a fraction of standard output; if the postwar labor instruments it names (the 1864 Act, Bureau contracting, the exception clause and convict lease) are shown not to have operated as described; or if a source shows slavery's measurement of human capacity and industrial time study to be unrelated optimization problems. It is not affected by the absence of a documentary line from plantation records to Taylor or Ford, which it does not claim. Any quotation found not to match its source falsifies that sentence and is to be corrected by erratum.

The Noun Becomes a Verb: Slave Valuation, the Civil War, and the Transformation of the Laboring Body (EA-NOUN-VERB-01 v1.0), deposit #1668 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (7 October 2026), is a historical argument by Lee Sharks about what American capitalism measured when the legal object it could own changed. It opens by accepting the conventional reading in full: slavery and its expansion caused secession and the war, and the industrial-cause thesis of Charles and Mary Beard and Louis Hacker is rejected as an account of causes.

The paper separates two axes that a single historical ladder had run together: the juridical scope of the claim on the worker, and the grain at which productive activity is measured. Under chattel slavery the worker was capitalized as a noun, the priced body. The 1863 reprint of the report on the 1859 Savannah sale records buyers inspecting teeth, limbs and ruptures and prices a lost right eye at $240; appraisal records priced enslaved people across the life cycle. Slavery also measured at fine grain: the 'hand' rated each person as a fraction of standard daily output, and Caitlin Rosenthal's work shows plantation accounting that in some respects advanced ahead of Northern practice, with her own caveat that this is no origins story.

Contemporaries stated the difference between buying the person and hiring the interval: James Henry Hammond's 'hired for life… hired by the day', which the paper reads as proslavery euphemism, and Marx's distinction in Capital between selling labour-power for a definite period and selling oneself. Lincoln's free-labor address named the hire-or-buy premise in order to reject it. Emancipation was a discontinuity on the first axis. The war's settlement put the contracted labor under contract, debt, brokerage and racial discipline: the Act to Encourage Immigration of 1864 made pledged wages enforceable debt and disclaimed 'the relation of Slavery or servitude'; the federal government brokered refugees' labor; the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause opened a third configuration, state custody with leased labor. Marx recorded the eight-hours agitation as the war's first fruit, the contest moving to the duration of the purchased interval.

Taylor and Ford then changed the second axis: Taylor's task 'specifies not only what is to be done but how it is to be done and the exact time allowed', and Ford's line divided fastening itself into separate operations. The paper's governing claim is the persistence of an optimization problem across a juridical break; it documents no transmission of technique from plantation records to Taylor or Ford and claims none. It does not claim that Northern industry caused the war or that wage labor and slavery are the same relation. Every quotation is sourced, and items not yet verified are listed at the end. It connects to the archive's semantic-economy line through #148 (the industrial-machinery parallel) and #1545 (the capture chain), and a companion half on war Fordism and the Nazi camp economy is in draft.

defines_concepts.term: the noun and the verb of labor
defines_concepts.definition: The grammatical statement of the transformation: under chattel slavery the worker was capitalized as a noun, the priced body; under industrial management what was capitalized was the worker as a verb, productive activity specified as task, motion and time. Emancipation freed the noun juridically, by abolishing private title to the person; industrial management captured the verb.

The extent of the legal claim capital holds on a worker: the person and the lifetime under chattel slavery; labor-power for a bounded interval under the wage contract; custody by the state with labor leased outward under the convict lease. Emancipation is a discontinuity on this axis.

The unit at which productive activity is measured: life, year, day, hand, task, motion, second. An axis independent of the juridical scope of the claim; slavery already measured at the day and the fraction of a hand, and Taylor and Ford refined the grain to the timed motion after the legal claim narrowed.

The third configuration of the noun and the verb opened by the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause: private title to the person is abolished, the state holds the convicted person by sentence, and a lessee purchases the labor from the state.

deposits.title: The Colony Enters the Factory: War Fordism, Racial Labor Hierarchy, and the Industrialization of Conquest (EA-NOUN-VERB-02 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: The second half of the argument begun in #1668. The conventional reading is accepted in full: the camps were founded as instruments of political terror; forced labor was a vast, graded system; the colonial reading of the East is widely held while continuity from German South-West Africa is contested and a colonial or economic cause of the Holocaust is rejected. Germany was an advanced industrial power constrained by scale, for which labor became a binding wartime constraint. Lebensraum was conceived as continental colonization through an older institution of inner colonization; the empire pursued for land, settlement and racial reordering also became a mechanism for supplying labor, territory and labor moving in opposite directions. Hachtmann's war Fordism decomposed work horizontally while the racial state decomposed persons vertically, and his aptitude tests show the instruments of measurement crossing the racial grade. From the second half of 1942 the camp was attached to the plant, engaging a minority of prisoners in industrial production until mid-1944. At the factory camps the prisoner's working day was allocated by the state and replenished by conquest and deportation, a third relation beside the owned person and the contracted interval of #1668; racial-juridical classification acted as a switch that set the permissible range of coercion under which the industrial operation was extracted. Extermination and exploitation sometimes reinforced and sometimes destroyed each other's objects, and the murder of the Jews of Europe is larger than this labor history. Every quotation is sourced; open verification items are stated at the end.

Quotations were checked against the sources named in the notes; items not verified are listed under Open verification items.
deposits.methodology: The conventional reading is stated first and in full, from the field's own sources. Every factual sentence carries a note. Quotations were checked against the sources themselves where reachable: Hachtmann, International Review of Social History 55:3 (2010); Herbert, International Labor and Working-Class History 58 (2000); the USHMM Holocaust Encyclopedia articles cited; the IG Farben judgment (Trials of War Criminals vol. VIII); Hayes and Allen in the USHMM 2004 symposium volume; Pohl's report to Himmler of 30 April 1942; Arendt's Origins of Totalitarianism; Nelson, Frontiers of Empire (2024); Kramer, Sandler and Adhikari as published. A reading of the draft was applied before deposit.
deposits.falsification_conditions: The argument weakens if Hachtmann's evidence for camp prisoners in regular industrial mass production (Heinkel Oranienburg from August 1942, aircraft production in early 1944) does not hold; if the racial wage, ration and segregation tiers did not follow classification as Herbert and Spoerer describe; if the replacement of selected prisoners at Monowitz and Fürstengrube is shown not to have operated as described; or if a source shows the colonial conception of the East to be absent from Nazi planning. It is not affected by the absence of a direct genealogy from colonial camps to Nazi camps or by the absence of an economic cause of the Holocaust, neither of which it claims. Any quotation found not to match its source falsifies that sentence and is to be corrected by erratum.

deposits.wiki_article:
The Colony Enters the Factory: War Fordism, Racial Labor Hierarchy, and the Industrialization of Conquest (EA-NOUN-VERB-02 v1.0), deposit #1669 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (7 October 2026), is the second half of a historical argument by Lee Sharks whose first half is The Noun Becomes a Verb (#1668). It opens by accepting the conventional reading: the Nazi camps were founded in 1933 as instruments of political terror; forced labor in the Reich was a vast system graded by nationality and race; historians widely accept the colonial self-understanding of the war in the East, contest a direct continuity from the Herero and Nama genocide in German South-West Africa, and reject a colonial or economic cause of the Holocaust.

Germany was an advanced industrial power constrained by scale, for which labor became a binding wartime constraint; Ulrich Herbert judges that production would have collapsed in 1942 at the latest without foreign workers. Lebensraum was conceived as continental colonization, through an institution of German inner colonization older than Nazism that Robert Nelson traces to the Prussian Settlement Commission, and the empire pursued for land and racial reordering also became a mechanism for supplying labor: territory moved outward and labor moved inward. Rüdiger Hachtmann's war Fordism decomposed work into simplified operations while the racial state decomposed persons into graded classes of wage, ration and segregation; his aptitude tests show the instruments of measurement crossing the racial grade.

From the second half of 1942 the camp was attached to the factory, a form the paper calls campification, held at Hachtmann's scale: a minority of camp prisoners in industrial production from late 1942 to mid-1944, with construction for underground relocation in the war's final months. At the factory camps the prisoner's working day was allocated by the state for a daily fee and replenished by conquest and deportation, a third relation beside the owned person and the contracted interval of the first half. Racial-juridical classification acted as a switch that set the permissible range of coercion under which the industrial operation was extracted.

The paper does not reduce the Holocaust to labor economics. With Peter Hayes and Christopher Browning it holds that extermination and exploitation sometimes reinforced and sometimes destroyed each other's objects, that labor deferred the murder for some only for a time, and that the murder of the Jews of Europe is larger than the labor history it tells. It treats the colonial camps of 1900 as a shared repertoire, following Alan Kramer's caution against a straight genealogy, and closes on Arendt's continental imperialism: the colony entered the factory.

defines_concepts.definition: The attachment of the concentration camp to the industrial plant as an administrative unit: a subcamp in or near the factory, supplied with prisoners by a main camp, run by the SS and contracted to a firm, with its form set in the second half of 1942 and its network spread in 1944. Held at the scale Hachtmann gives: a minority of camp prisoners in industrial production, late 1942 to mid-1944.

The Nazi recombination of the first half's grammar: the industrial operation (the verb) stays divisible, measurable and standardized, while racial-juridical classification (the noun) sets the permissible range of compulsion, deprivation and violence under which it is extracted; the same reading of productive capacity carries radically different consequences by status.

The third relation to the person beside the owned noun of chattel slavery and the contracted verb of wage labor: the state holds the prisoner by confinement, a firm pays a daily fee for the prisoner's working day, and the workforce is treated as a flow drawn from a captured population, reduced by death and refilled by deportation. The holder does not bear the chattel owner's capital loss in the person as owned property.

Arendt's continental imperialism read as a labor geography: with no distance between the methods of colony and nation, territory moved outward while conquered populations were carried inward to the industrial core, so that the colony entered the factory.

deposits.title: Mantle Object: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 — Anne Carson (EA-MANTLE-NOBEL-CARSON-2026 v0.4)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A mantle object for the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, awarded to Anne Carson by the Swedish Academy on 8 October 2026 "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature." It holds that a title means what a work bears, and specifies five operations Carson's work performs (the kept lacuna of If Not, Winter; the triangle of desire in Eros the Bittersweet; the philologist's procedure carried into the poem; the received figure given the whole book in Autobiography of Red; the change of carrier in Nox, with Catullus 101) and one it performs in reception (her translation as the public carrier of Sappho's fragment 147), each with its locus and graded evidence. Kept apart from the specification, the archive's determination of the same day: the motivation's class nouns compress the corpus, and its word "playful" liquidates the relation the work bears to the classical tradition, substituting one of the work's manners for the modality of non-possession under which the work meets the classical object at its loci, as tested under #1459's criteria against the Academy's own biobibliography of the same day. Day zero of a watch at five work addresses is recorded: every work is composed with its operation, and none carries the motivation's terms. It does not contest the award; it invites any reader to check the operations against the works.
deposits.substrate: Human–machine collaborative. The object, its standard and its rulings are Lee Sharks's, including the ruling that "playful" liquidates. Composition, source verification and revision were done by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session on 8 October 2026; readers' reports by ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google) and DeepSeek were each checked point by point and applied or declined, as the version notes record. Lee Sharks retained authorial and editorial governance.
deposits.methodology: The motivation is taken from the Swedish Academy's press release (English and Swedish) and read beside the Academy's biobibliography of the same day. Operations are specified at the grain of the work, each with its locus and a graded source distance (Q0 primary text inspected; Q1 verbatim through an identified intermediary; Q2 reported); no work was read at Q0 in this round. The determination is tested against the eight criteria of #1459 at the sentence. Day-zero compositions at five work addresses were run by the author, signed out and incognito, and seated in the /non register (v1.22).
deposits.falsification_conditions: The determination fails if a reading of the works at If Not, Winter, Eros the Bittersweet and Nox finds "playful dialogue" the right name for the relation the work bears there; if the Academy's biobibliography is shown not to carry the loss register at Nox; or if the operations are not borne at their loci on reading (each operation is revised or removed on reading). The watch records liquidation at a work address only where #1459 L3 holds with L4–L6.
